_about: signalbox's resource ledger: what the box has, the headroom, the classes and their ranks, the class slices and the tape's cpus. tools/signalbox/ledger.py loads it once at start and refuses a file it cannot read, a key it does not know, a rank order that breaks the user's order or a tape cpu list that is not what its pool occupies (daemon.py --check validates a copy before a restart; tools/boxres/boxres.py reads the same file). Every number has a <name>_why beside it that says where it comes from; the loader ignores the comments. Install: cp configs/box-resources.json /home/user/signalbox/box-resources.json.

ram.os_other_bytes_why: What the OS holds that no job owns: bloomery's OS_OTHER (crates/placement workstation.rs), read with free -b on the box, 6,694,629,376 B = 6.69 GB [measured]. G = MemTotal - max(this, unowned) - headroom, with unowned = (MemTotal - MemAvailable) - the holders' measured resident.
ram.headroom_bytes_why: H = 4 GiB [derived]: zone watermarks about 0.6 GB (min_free_kbytes 66 MiB, watermark_scale_factor 10, 251 GiB), page tables of a 99 GB mapping about 0.19 GB (24.2 M PTEs x 8 B), HOST_DRIFT 0.5 GiB, slab growth; about 1.4 GB named, taken x3. Accepted as the start (lead, 2026-10-20).
ram.memory_high_factor_why: A unit's MemoryHigh = this x its resident need: it is throttled before it is stopped. Accepted as the start (lead, 2026-10-20). MemoryHigh and MemoryMax bind on a cgroup's charge, and a file page is charged to the cgroup that first read it: a model file read before the unit started (a download in an ssh session's user.slice) is not throttled by a fresh slice.
ram.memory_max_factor_why: MemoryMax = this x the resident need + memory_max_add_bytes: an under-declarer is stopped inside its own cgroup, never a neighbour. Accepted as the start (lead, 2026-10-20); same charge rule as memory_high_factor.
ram.memory_max_add_bytes_why: 2 GiB: the process image and its stacks, which a resident-set declaration (the plan's page classes) does not count. Accepted as the start (lead, 2026-10-20).

grants.appear_s_why: A grant is posted before its owner exists (the client asks, then starts the unit): this long for the unit or pid to show up before the grant is expired and named. Design round boxres, 2026-10-20, case 'a grant whose unit never appears within 30 s'.
grants.history_why: Ended grants kept in state.json for /ledger's recent list: the last 200 decisions, as the design asks (docs: design round boxres, section 9).
grants.idle_card_s_why: A grant that holds a card while the card shows 0 % utilization this long is named `held` in /ledger (a forgotten serve, a hung run); nothing is stopped. 10 min, the design's case 'a card holder at 0 % SM for 10 min' (design round boxres, 2026-10-20, section 7). A chosen threshold, not a measurement; 0 turns the word off.
grants.overdue_factor_why: A grant that declared expected_s and has run past this many times it is named `overdue` in /ledger (the unit's own RuntimeMaxSec, from boxres run --bound, is what stops it). 2, the design's case 'unit alive past 2 x expected_s' (design round boxres, section 7). A chosen threshold, not a measurement; 0 turns the word off.

cpus.all_why: 4 CCDs x (8 cores + 8 SMT siblings) = 64 logical CPUs; CCD k has primaries 8k..8k+7 and siblings 32+8k..32+8k+7 (lscpu -e on the box, 2026-10-20). Grants name their cpus as explicit lists, siblings included.
cpus.ccds_why: 4 CCDs [read: lscpu -e on the box, 2026-10-20; CCD k = L3 group k]. The pool's spread rule needs it.
cpus.cores_per_ccd_why: 8 primary cores a CCD: CCD k has primaries 8k..8k+7 [read: lscpu -e on the box, 2026-10-20].
cpus.smt_offset_why: A core's SMT sibling is the core + 32: siblings are 32+8k..32+8k+7 on CCD k [read: lscpu -e on the box, 2026-10-20].

nvme0.mount_why: nvme0n1p1 is /models (3.7 TB): the files gates, benches and serving read [read: findmnt, 2026-10-20].

nvme1.mount_why: nvme1n1p2 is / (980 PRO 2 TB): cargo targets and the download workshop /home/user/stage [read: findmnt, 2026-10-20].

classes.sitting_why: The timing sitting is the top: the user's order (2026-10-20) is timing sitting > media and the release pass > toktape > landing batch > round batch > static tier > downloads. It owns the box (exclusive) and is the drain barrier for every lower class, media included. The design's 950 media / 900 sitting is swapped by that order.
classes.media_why: Media (ltx, img, music, echo takes and ComfyUI windows) sits below the sitting and level with the release pass; the jobs keep their own semantics (ahead of the queue, preempting nothing, holding their card).
classes.release_why: The release pass (the user-facing pass and the union batch before a tag) is level with media: user order, 2026-10-20.
classes.tape_why: The toktape recording: below media and release, above every batch. Design round boxres, class 'tape' 800.
classes.lead_why: The landing batch (the lead's jobs): unchanged from the live CLASS_PRIORITY.
classes.round_why: The round batch (gates and builds a round queues): unchanged from the live CLASS_PRIORITY.
classes.static_why: The static tier (rounds.slice units): below the round batch. Design round boxres, class 'static' 300.
classes.fill_why: Downloads, requants and idle fill: unchanged from the live CLASS_PRIORITY.

slices._about: Class -> the slice unit a queued job of that class (signalbox) or a boxres run starts in. A class not listed runs where it ran before (system.slice for a queued job, the caller's cgroup for boxres). The caps live in each slice's own unit file in configs/ and nowhere else; the per-unit caps (MemoryHigh, MemoryMax, AllowedCPUs) come from the grant's need. A slice that is not installed (systemctl show: FragmentPath empty) is refused by name, rc 69: systemd makes an implicit slice with no caps out of any name, so LoadState=loaded says nothing.
slices.round_why: The round batch's gates and builds: configs/boxres-round.slice. A dash in a slice name makes boxres.slice its implicit parent.
slices.static_why: The static tier's rounds.slice (configs/rounds.slice: CCDs 2-3, half weight, the 40G/56G caps); the design makes it the static class's slice (design round boxres, sections 6 and 8), so its caps are spelled in that one file.
slices.fill_why: Downloads, requants and idle fill: configs/boxres-fill.slice. A fill unit's page cache is charged to the unit, so its MemoryHigh keeps a download from filling the page cache that holds an unlocked host set.

tape._about: The toktape recording on the 3090 with the host tier: what boxres run --class tape defaults to. The lists are held by the loader against the pool rule they are derived from (ledger.pool_cpus), so a comment cannot drift from them.
tape.hold_why: The hold boxres run --class tape writes, /root/bloomery-tape-hold with pid= and start=: bloomery's lease_guard makes every direct tools/box.sh call wait while it exists (its owner passes with BLOOMERY_HOLD_OWNER=tape). Design round boxres, section 5, row 'direct tools/box.sh call'.
tape.threads_why: BLOOMERY_THREADS=24 for the recording, so eight cores stay whole for the rounds (design round boxres, section 4.3). Whether 24 keeps the host leg within 5 % of 32 is the open term the boxres-t24 card measures (predicted 0 % to -15 % [derived]); until then boxres run --threads N (or --cpus) overrides: --threads 32 holds every cpu and drains the rounds.
tape.cpus_why: What 24 pool workers occupy [derived]: worker t sits on CCD t mod 4 as that CCD's t div 4 -th core, primaries first (bloomery crates/threads/src/lib.rs ccd_slot and cpu_for), so t=0..23 take primaries 0-5, 8-13, 16-21, 24-29, and their SMT siblings (+32) are 32-37, 40-45, 48-53, 56-61. The siblings are held too so no round shares a tape worker's core. To verify on the box after a start: every task of the serve has a Cpus_allowed_list inside this list.
tape.rounds_cpus_why: What the rounds keep beside the tape [derived]: the box's 64 cpus less the tape's 48, one core pair (6-7, 14-15, 22-23, 30-31) and its siblings (+32) a CCD, whole cores with no SMT sharing with a tape worker. 8 cores / 16 threads, so a box-static build runs on 8 cores instead of 16 (design round boxres, section 4.3).
tape.nvme_why: The tape reads its row table's 4 KiB rows from /models (nvme0) while it decodes: a latency holder, so nvme0 bulk IO (downloads, requant moves) is refused while it runs (design round boxres, sections 3 and 4.4).
tape.oom_score_adj_why: The recording's locked pages make it the OOM killer's first pick under global pressure; -900 puts it last short of -1000 (design round boxres, section 4.2). Written by boxres into the process before it execs.
